ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a light-yellow shaded triangle. Its short horizontal base on the right is labeled 5 in., and the upper slanted side is labeled 21.5 in. From the upper-left vertex downward there is a pink dashed vertical segment, labeled 8 in.; then to the right there is a pink dashed horizontal segment, labeled 15 in., and the two dashed lines form a right angle. These two dashed lines correspond to the two legs of a right triangle, and its hypotenuse is the other slanted side of the shaded triangle. Reasoning: First find the length of the unlabeled slanted side of the shaded triangle: sqrt(8^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(64 + 225) = sqrt(289) = 17 in. Therefore the perimeter of the shaded triangle is 21.5 + 17 + 5 = 43.5 in.

raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of the triangle. Round to the nearest tenth if necessary.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a shaded triangle whose base is the horizontal segment labeled 5 in, whose upper slanted side is labeled 21.5 in, and whose lower slanted side runs from the upper-left vertex down to the left end of the 5-in base. Use the dashed vertical 8 in and dashed horizontal 15 in as the perpendicular legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is that lower slanted side. Compute the missing side by the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(8^2+15^2)=17. Then add the three triangle sides: 21.5+17+5=43.5.
